name: Shinobi
description: Network video recorder for IP cameras (RTSP/ONVIF). Listed with manual setup only: upstream publishes no versioned images and its licence restricts commercial use.
license: Shinobi Open Source Software License Agreement (free for personal and non-commercial use; not OSI-approved)
installNote: Not installable from the catalog yet. Shinobi publishes only moving image tags (dev, latest) on its GitLab registry, so no version can be pinned and re-installed identically; its default image embeds MariaDB in the application container; and its licence requires a paid subscription for commercial use or 15+ cameras. Follow the official Docker guide, then adopt the Compose project here to manage, back up and route it.
manualSetup: Follow https://docs.shinobi.video/installation/docker with your own Compose file (map /home/Shinobi/videos to a Docker volume or a dedicated folder).
Change the superuser login at /super immediately, then create the administrator account there.
Add cameras by their RTSP address; ONVIF discovery needs multicast, which Docker Desktop does not pass.
Adopt the Compose project on the Installed apps page to back it up and route it.
limitations: Only moving tags (dev, latest) are published; a digest pin cannot be updated by version.
Camera discovery (ONVIF multicast) does not work through Docker Desktop; enter camera addresses manually.
Recording many cameras needs significant disk throughput and CPU; Docker Desktop on Windows is suitable for testing only.

notes: The mobile app and API keys need direct access: protect only the browser interface.
